approvals.approval: Place of Entertainment, Limited Live Performance or Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit

basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Regular amplified sound outdoors needs a Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound permit. The Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on each application. Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit, and dancing by patrons needs no permit of its own. Where a permit is needed: further review.
basis.code_section: San Francisco Police Code § 1060 et seq. (Place of Entertainment; Limited Live Performance; Fixed Place Outdoor Amplified Sound)

comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved in 2008. Planning's note—'Approval does not establish a new bar use'—signals that continuation of an existing restaurant with Type 41 is treated differently than establishing a new bar, even in the SUD.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 66 meters away on Valencia in NCT-VALENCIA, same SUD. CUA for 'Bar within Full Service Restaurant' filed 2010, cancelled before hearing in 2011—a use decision that did not reach approval or denial.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Cancellation (not withdrawal) of a bar-within-restaurant CUA 66 m away shows that applicants sometimes abandon bar proposals in this corridor before a hearing, possibly due to neighborhood concerns or SUD constraints. No conditions are on record.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 210 meters away at 2519 Mission in NCT-MISSION (adjacent SUD block). CUA for retail-to-restaurant change of use with Type 41 license, live entertainment and arts activities. Filed 2019, withdrawn before decision in October 2019.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Applicant withdrew a Type 41 restaurant + live entertainment CUA on Mission Street within three months of filing. The record does not state a reason, but withdrawal of a similar concept (food + beer/wine + live music) nearby is a caution flag.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 178 meters away in NCT-VALENCIA, within the SUD corridor. CUA to add live entertainment to Club American (a bar). Filed 1993, withdrawn 1993.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: A 1993 CUA to add live entertainment to an existing bar was withdrawn before decision, showing that entertainment additions to bars have historically faced hurdles in this district, though the record does not state the reason.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 152 meters away at 2512 Mission in NCT-MISSION. Planning approved an Entertainment Commission referral for a Place of Entertainment permit at Arcana, a restaurant with nighttime entertainment use, in 2020.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: 94 meters away at 1034 Valencia in NCT-VALENCIA. Planning denied an EC referral in 2015 for a Limited Live Performance permit as accessory to a retail video store (Lost Weekend Video).

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Valencia Street in NCT-VALENCIA, within the Mission Alcohol SUD. Planning approved continuation of an existing bar license in 2006 with a condition prohibiting expansion of the bar square footage or substantial change in mode or character of operation.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm the SUD license-transfer requirement with SF Planning in writing: ask whether Planning Code § 249.60(b)(2)(C) requires a Type 42 bar license to be transferred from another bar within the SUD, or only Type 47/48 full-bar licenses.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email or visit the Planning Department zoning counter and ask: 'We are proposing a beer-and-wine bar (ABC Type 42) at 995 Valencia St in the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD. Planning Code § 249.60(b)(2)(C) requires a new bar to use a license transferred from another bar within the SUD. Does that requirement apply to a Type 42 license, or only to Type 47/48 full-bar licenses? If it applies, can you confirm in writing which ABC license types from which premises within the SUD would satisfy it?' Keep the written answer with your CUA application.

filing_playbook.action: Once the CUA is approved, email the Entertainment Commission Deputy Director to confirm whether the live entertainment as described requires a Place of Entertainment permit, then file the appropriate application.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Describe the concept: 'We will have occasional live music (solo or duo acoustic guitar, vocals) with amplification, two to three nights per week, ending by 10 or 11 p.m., in a 40-seat bar.' File the application the Commission confirms, pay the fee ($2,708 for POE in 2026–27), and discuss the posted notice.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: File the building permit application with DBI through the PermitSF portal, including the architectural plans stamped by a licensed architect and the tenant improvement scope (kitchen, bar, restrooms, ADA, finishes).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: In the permit application, state: 'Tenant improvements to convert existing restaurant space to a bar use (40 seats, limited cooking). Change of use approved by Planning Commission CUA [motion number]. Work includes new bar millwork, limited kitchen equipment (panini press, refrigeration, three-compartment sink), ADA-compliant restroom upgrades, new finishes, electrical and plumbing per attached plans.' Request routing to Planning, Public Health, Fire, and PUC. Expect 2–4 months for plan review.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline is 240–540 days to approval of the Conditional Use Authorization, Place of Entertainment permit, ABC Type 42 license, Health permit and Building permit, measured from first filing to the last approval. The CUA alone takes 120–300 days from filing to Commission approval (catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization); the POE permit takes 45–120 days after the CUA is approved (catalog:sf.place_of_entertainment_permit); the ABC Type 42 application takes 60–150 days if unprotested, longer if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required due to census tract undue concentration (catalog:ca.abc_type_42); the Health plan check takes 21–60 days and the permit to operate another 14–45 days after final inspection (catalog:sf.health_plan_check, catalog:sf.health_permit); the Building permit takes 14–120 days for plan review and issuance (catalog:sf.building_permit). These approvals run partly in parallel (ABC and building permits can be filed after the CUA is approved, and the health permit after DPH plan check), so the total elapsed time to open is roughly 8–18 months if all approvals are granted. Cost includes CUA filing fee $3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost (catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization), POE permit $2,708–$3,800 (catalog:sf.place_of_entertainment_permit), ABC Type 42 application $1,000–$1,600 (catalog:ca.abc_type_42), DPH plan check $828–$2,500 and permit to operate $470–$1,000 (catalog:sf.health_plan_check, catalog:sf.health_permit), building permit $800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation (catalog:sf.building_permit), business registration $55–$700 (catalog:sf.business_registration), sign permit $300–$1,500 (catalog:sf.sign_permit), and state fees (entity registration $70–$150, seller's permit $0, EDD registration $0, food safety manager cert $100–$250, RBS training $3–$30 per employee). The cost range does not include the price of purchasing and transferring an ABC Type 42 license from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD if Planning confirms that is required; license transfer prices are not government fees and are not included in the catalog. It also does not include architecture, construction, a license broker, or legal fees. The timeline and cost are for approvals when they are granted; if the CUA or ABC license is denied or the applicant withdraws, the time and cost to that point are lost.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St is zoned NCT-VALENCIA where a bar is a conditional use requiring a Conditional Use Authorization. The site sits inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which requires any new bar to use a liquor license transferred from another bar already located within the SUD—a significant constraint. The pathway shows this is a change of use from Restaurant to Bar (an active Type 41 license is on file for Sarita's Grill & Beer). The immediate area is dense: 24 food/drink businesses and 9 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, flagged for undue concentration. Very few comparable bar decisions exist nearby: only 1 approved, 0 denied, 2 withdrawn in the last 10 years within 1,000 ft—too few to calculate an approval rate.
